newsitem.title: UK: Saatchi's new New York CEO to push creative focus.
newsitem.headline: Saatchi's new New York CEO to push creative focus.

text.p: Jennifer Laing, the newly appointed chief executive officer for Saatchi & Saatchi, North America, said Thursday she expects to take some of the advertising agency's London culture with her to the more conservative New York office.
"New York is the biggest office in the Saatchi network," Laing told Reuters in an interview. "New York has the scale, the size. London has the heartbeat."

Saatchi & Saatchi, part of Cordiant Plc, Thursday said it named Laing as CEO of its North American operation. Alan Bishop, the current CEO for North America, will assume Laing's position as chairman of Saatchi & Saatchi, London.

Saatchi & Saatchi has been rocked by change over recent months. John Fitzgerald, who was named president and chief operating officer of Saatchi & Saatchi Worldwide in early 1996 and was assumed to be the heir apparent to chairman Ed Wax, was ousted from the agency in early August.

Laing -- who sharply denied any suggestions that Saatchi & Saatchi and Cordiant are continuing to suffer from the ouster almost two years ago of founder and chairman Maurice Saatchi -- said that in addition to looking after clients, she will tackle the creative side.

Laing worked for Saatchi & Saatchi for 17 years before forming an agency herself that was then bought by Cordiant in early 1995. She was circumspect in talking about any specific goals, repeatedly saying it is premature to make any assessments until she is working in New York.

"The whole thing is about tranferring best practice from office to office around the network," she said of her swapping positions with Bishop. "That is something that clients do all the time and agencies do less of.

"I'm sure that Alan will bring to London some American business practices, and I will bring some Saatchi culture," she said. Saatchi culture, she said, has "to do with single-minded strategic thought, with brave, memorable executions."
Saatchi & Saatchi's North American clients include General Mills, Procter & Gamble, Gillette and Campbell Soup.
"The client base (in New York) is different," she said. "There are fewer, bigger clients. While we have a longer list of clients in London. That may require a different kind of approach."
Smaller accounts generally are willing to take more creative risks than large, established businesses.
Laing, who will assume the new post on Jan. 1, said the financial nuts and bolts will not be her concern. "That's not my priority," she said.
"The (profit) margin is fine in America. ... My priority has always been, and always will be, clients, clients and clients. One thing I need to do is make sure that all the clients are being helped.
